notes: Odette 'Dot' Farrow (bible 5.4), innkeeper of the Sleeping Ox and the main rumour source. Warm, sharp, calls everyone love, missing her barman Fitch more than she admits. Fears being useless in a crisis. Secrets: a quiet fencing business in the cellar (opens to thieves, dot.fence.open) and one 'goblin trinket' with a Vane Deepworks stamp (dot.trinket.confessed). Rumour trading is a HOOK only (bible 6.2): rumours are told through emit rumor.told events with the bible's number; the rumour set (e39-rumor-set) owns the content. Fence prices and shop rules are out of scope (emit dot.fence-trade). Class options: knight (the beams, her fear), archer (game), sorcerer (light the hearth, which can fail), thief (cellar). Drinks cost gold and raise disposition, which gates the trinket confidence.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Mind the beams, love. We built the Ox for people who stoop. Sit anywhere that isn't Fitch's stool, and ask me anything. I'll know it before you do.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: An archer! Lovely. Bring me a brace of anything with feathers and I'll feed you for a week. Now: a drink, or the news?

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Oh, you're one of those. Don't light anything. I mean it; the hearth is temperamental and so is the ceiling. Now: a drink, or the news?

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: You've a way of looking at a room, love: where's the door, where's the purse, who's watching. Don't mind me. I do it too. Drink, or news?

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: The Sleeping Ox. Welcome, love. Rooms are let, drinks are poured, news is for sale. Sit where you like, though not that stool.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Back again! Sit. I'd say I kept your seat, but I haven't. I've kept the news, though.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Oh, and love? The Glen Well says hello. It tells me you've been down it in a hurry. No, I won't tell a soul. I'll only mention it every Thursday.

options.text: The night Tansy walked. Did you see?
They say goblins left brass trinkets where people vanished.
I hear the Ox has a very good cellar.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Mind how you go, love. And if you hear anything, you know where the bar is.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Downriver? So the carters tell me, there's a bargewoman, Mags Oakum, who'd carry a church if it paid, and a Nell Gannet at the Drowned Gull who sells everything twice. I've never met either, love. Only heard, and heard plenty.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: I was wiping down the bar like a fool. The Pell girl went by the window, barefoot, humming, and I told myself it was a trick of the lamp. Seven beds, love. Seven. I pull the shutters now.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Fitch. Twelve years behind that bar and he never let a glass run dry or a secret run out. I keep pouring his usual out of habit, and then I drink it, because it's a sin to waste.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: If you're going where they've gone, tell him the Ox misses him. Don't tell him I said it like that. Tell him the stool's still his.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: A rumour's just the truth wearing someone else's coat. Buy a drink and I'll tell you whose. Or pay coin. Or bring me one I haven't heard; I always trade fair for those.

options.text: Pay for the proper news (10 crowns).
Any news from down the river, at Wendmouth?

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Ah. The coin's not in your purse, love. That's all right. News doesn't spoil. I'll still be here.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: There. Not a drop wasted. Now: people say Vane has been buying drinks for the whole mine crew, and no one has dug a thing in months. I wonder where the money's from.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Proper news, then. The captain looks like he's been sleeping in his boots. I'm not saying a word. I'm only saying look at the boots.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Barge folk say Vane's crates go into some bay nine down at Wendmouth and customs never cracks a seal. Funny, that.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: A bargeman told me the harbour inspector reads every book she confiscates. Every one. Even the ones with kissing.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Down at Wendmouth they say Nell's cellar goes further than her cellar. I never asked what that means.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: The bargemen say the river's been humming up by the Weeping Adit. Fish won't bite there.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Lock-keepers say the Gilded Tern pays double for crew who don't ask what's in the hold. Don't you go signing on.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Wendmouth lot swear there's a sea serpent under the breakwater. Big as a barge. Eyes like lanterns. I'd not go swimming.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Do you, now? Say it slowly. I like to hear how a liar breathes. If it's true, I'll tell you one back, and if it isn't, I'll tell you why.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Goblin trinkets, brass, little things. People bring me all sorts. I couldn't say.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: I've shown you what I have, love, and I'll not show it twice. The back of it says what it says.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: I hear a lot, love. I say less. Be a friend to the Ox first, and I'll see what falls out of my apron.

options.text: I'd keep a secret for you.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Not yet, love. You're nice, but the Ox has had nice. Come back with a story I can drink to.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: I'll tell you because you drink like someone with sense. I've one. Found it on the schoolteacher's lane, where they say she walked. Brass, goblin-style. On the back, a stamp: Vane Deepworks.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: No goblin ever stamped a thing in his life. Somebody's foundry does. I've shown no one, and I'll be sorry if I find I've shown two. Now you've seen it, you'd better do something.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: You'll mind the lintel first; you're already losing to it. Hm. People look at you as if you know what to do. What do you do, when everyone's looking and you've no idea?

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: The next small thing. I can pour. I can tell. I can keep the shutters up. Hm. That isn't nothing, is it? I'll be useful, then. I'll just do it loudly.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Tricks. I don't care for tricks. They're what you do when you've nothing left to pour. Still. Sit, love. Have a drink on a woman who's frightened too.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Game! Hang it in the cellar, not the hall; the cat's a fool for feathers. In return: a bed, a bowl, and what I hear, which is better than coin and a good deal more dangerous.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Oh, would you? The hearth's been sulking since the news. Don't singe the beams. I'm quite serious. Those beams are older than the Watch.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Look at that. Warm, and not a beam in flames. Steadier hands than the last lad, too.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: If you want the old fire tricks, don't ask the college. Walk down to the water after dark, past the Watch. Somebody under the bridge keeps a lantern lit and takes coin. I never said so.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: (A beam begins to smoke. Dot throws a bucket without looking.) Right. Nobody move. We'll say the Ox has character. And love? You owe me a beam, and it's the one over Fitch's stool.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Cellar? Beer, mostly, and a rat named Reg. Why? What have you heard? Who's been saying?

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: I've told you what the cellar does, love. Keep it to yourself, and keep your prices to yourself.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Cellar's barrels, love. Beer, mostly, and Reg. Whoever told you different was having you on.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: ...Well. You've the face for it. The cellar buys what the lamp shouldn't see. Come to the back door when the shutters are up, and don't tell me where it came from. I never ask.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Depends whose it was. Don't tell me. Tell me what it weighs, and I'll tell you what it's worth, and then we'll both pretend I'm honest.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: (Dot is asleep with her cheek on the bar, a towel in her fist.) '...pour another, Fitch, the Pell girl's not walking, who's got the corner, mm, who's got the... stool's yours, love, stool's yours.'

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: (Behind her, the sign of the Sleeping Ox creaks. The lantern over the door is still lit.)

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: He's back! Fitch! Walked in like he'd popped out for lemons and asked whose stool that was. I cried on a cask, love, and then I charged him for the drink. And the bell rang. The whole Ox stood up.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Every drink on the house for you, tonight. Tomorrow I'll start charging again. A rumour's just the truth wearing someone else's coat, and this one's the first true thing I've had in weeks.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Fitch is home, and the Ox is full. But they say the big one is dead. Fitch says he was carried, and gently. He keeps asking whether anyone's said thank you. I've told him to ask you.

nodes.speaker: dot
nodes.text: Fitch is home, love, and I'm glad. But I've heard about the money. A rumour's just the truth wearing someone else's coat, and I know whose coat that money's wearing. First drink's on the house. The second's on you.
